issues.display_title: Issue #2033: investigate(payment): analyze why plan changes are permitted when subscription status is inactive or past_due
issues.main_description_html:
Objective

Investigate and document the root causes of why the backend allows users with inactive or past-due subscriptions to initiate subscription plan change requests (upgrades/downgrades), leading to failed transactions and unhandled exceptions in cc_logs.

Context & Evidence

  • Triggering Case: User 987 (jimmy.hellenis@gmail.com) experienced consecutive plan change failures logged in ccdb.cc_logs (log_id: 108374 & 108385) with error Failed to retrieve subscription: messages.tours.subscription_not_active.
  • Underlying State: User's Stripe subscription (sub_1ME1A64UXotNjjkI4TAkcz6i) is in past_due status due to failed recurring charges, yet plan change operations reached the Stripe modification layer.

Investigation Scope

  1. Status API Evaluation (GET /v2/payment/subscription/status):
    • Examine how GetSubStatus.php queries Stripe and PayPal subscriptions.
    • Investigate why the endpoint returns subscription: true and a valid nextPayment date regardless of whether the subscription is active, past_due, unpaid, or canceled.
  2. Subscription Lifecycle & Database State:
    • Investigate whether the GoThru database (gothru_mod.users / user_extra_data) is informed or updated when Stripe webhooks / dunning cycles emit invoice payment failures (invoice.payment_failed / subscription status changes).
    • Trace how inactive subscriptions are represented across DB tables versus actual Stripe/PayPal status.
  3. Guard Logic in Plan Change Handlers:
    • Review pre-condition validation in Upgrade.php, Downgrade.php, and PaymentHelpers.php.
    • Identify where and when subscription health should be evaluated before attempting modifications.
  4. Error Handling & Localization Audit:
    • Trace why messages.tours.subscription_not_active is thrown as a raw key and why DowngradeHelper logs from: unknown when Stripe retrieval fails.

Deliverables

  • A comprehensive investigation summary detailing the state flow between Stripe/PayPal, the DB, and the API endpoints.
  • Technical recommendations and action items for gating plan change requests when subscription status is not active.

Result

  • Investigation Document: docs/investigations/2026-10-10-issue-2033-plan-change-past-due-root-cause-analysis.md
  • Pull Requests:
    • Initial Document: GoThru-API-New #2048 (Merged)
    • Streamlined Update: GoThru-API-New #2049 (Open)
  • Core Findings & Root Cause:
    • User Was Unaware Due to Unhandled UI: User 987 was in dunning status (past_due) in Stripe, but attempted to change plan. There is a high probability the user was unaware because previously the UI did not handle this state (no warning/banner was shown, and Upgrade/Downgrade buttons were active).
    • Backend Validation Rejection: The backend blocked the modification in accordance with Stripe billing rules (subscriptions must be active to change tiers, preventing compounded debt). Because the action was not blocked at the UI layer, it resulted in failed transaction logs.
  • Current Status:
    • This flow is now already handled:
      • GET /v2/payment/subscription/status now exposes is_past_due and overdue amounts.
      • Frontend UI now disables Upgrade/Downgrade buttons during dunning and guides the user to Billing ([Go to Billing]).
      • Updating card details now triggers instant invoice payment to restore the account to active.

issues.display_title: Issue #2034: feat(payment): expose failed payment status and billing method in subscription status endpoint
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

When a subscriber's recurring card renewal fails on Stripe, their subscription enters an overdue (past due) state. Currently, the subscription status endpoint always reports the account as active, so the dashboard cannot detect when a renewal has failed.

Scope of Work

  • Update the subscription status response to include real-time payment status (is_past_due, subscription status).
  • Include the subscription's billing collection method (charge_automatically vs send_invoice) so the frontend can display the appropriate guidance.
  • Ensure all existing status fields remain backward-compatible.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Subscription status response accurately indicates whether the account has an overdue renewal payment.
  • Response indicates the billing collection method.
  • Active subscribers continue to see normal active status with zero interruption.

Result

  • Pull Requests:
    • #2036 (Merged) — Expose dunning status (is_past_due, status, collection_method)
    • #2038 (Merged) — Restrict is_past_due evaluation strictly to past_due and unpaid (excluding incomplete initial signup status)
  • Key Commits:
    • 02d7c3432 — Initial contract payload update in GetSubStatus.php
    • 090c3d5b4 — Restrict is_past_due check to renewal dunning statuses
  • Implementation:
    • Updated GetSubStatus.php to extract Stripe subscription status and collection method into API payload.
    • Exposes is_past_due: boolean, status: string, and collection_method: string.
  • Verification:
    • Tested across active, past_due, and send_invoice subscription states.

issues.display_title: Issue #2035: feat(payment): automatically charge pending renewal invoice upon card update
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

When an overdue subscriber updates their credit/debit card, the system saves the new card but does not attempt to settle the unpaid renewal invoice. As a result, the account remains in an overdue state for several days until Stripe's background retry runs.

Scope of Work

  • When an auto-charge subscriber updates their card details, immediately trigger payment for their pending renewal invoice.
  • If the payment succeeds, restore the subscription to active status immediately.
  • If the new card is declined by the bank, return a clear, user-friendly error explaining the decline reason.
  • Skip automatic charging for legacy manual-invoice accounts to prevent unintended charges.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Entering a valid new card instantly settles the overdue renewal invoice and reactivates the subscription.
  • If the new card is declined, the user receives an informative error message.
  • Manual-invoice (send_invoice) accounts are not charged automatically.

Result

  • Pull Requests:
    • #2036 (Merged) — Synchronous renewal re-charge on card update & bank decline mapping
    • #2037 (Merged) — Explicitly pass new card source to Stripe invoice payment & add structured logging
    • #2038 (Merged) — Exclude incomplete signup status from dunning auto-pay eligibility
    • #2039 (Merged) — Safe race condition handling for concurrent Stripe Smart Retries (invoice_already_paid)
    • #2040 (Merged) — Return transaction settlement payload (invoice_settled, invoice_id, amount_paid, currency) for frontend feedback
  • Key Commits:
    • 02d7c3432 — Core synchronous invoice pay in EditCardAction
    • b81bf6854 — Explicit source passing & warning logger
    • 090c3d5b4 — Restrict auto-pay to past_due and unpaid
    • 0b32e3da6 — Catch concurrent InvalidRequestException: invoice_already_paid
    • fc1bcc814 — Return settlement details array from EditCardAction
  • Implementation:
    • Integrated CardRepository::payInvoice() into EditCardAction::attemptAutoPayPastDueInvoice().
    • Mapped CardPaymentDeclinedException to HTTP 422 for clear feedback.
    • Return transaction details (invoice_settled, invoice_id, amount_paid, currency) to allow frontend to distinguish ordinary card updates from renewal settlements.
  • Verification:
    • Unit test suite (tests/Actions/Payment/EditCardActionTest.php): 11/11 tests passed (15 assertions, 100%).

issues.display_title: Issue #2041: feat(payment): expose outstanding renewal invoice amount and currency in subscription status endpoint
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

When an overdue subscriber views the billing update modal on the dashboard, the frontend needs to display an alert box with the exact overdue balance (e.g., "$34.00 USD") so the user knows what amount will be charged upon card update. Currently, the subscription status endpoint only returns boolean is_past_due: true without the pending invoice balance.

Scope of Work

  • In GetSubStatus.php, expand latest_invoice when retrieving the Stripe subscription details ($stripe->subscriptions->retrieve($recurringProfile, ['expand' => ['latest_invoice']])).
  • If the subscription is in dunning (past_due or unpaid), extract amount_due (converted from cents to currency units) and uppercase currency from latest_invoice.
  • Include amount_due (nullable float) and currency (nullable string) in the encrypted response payload $rowDatas.
  • Maintain backward compatibility for active subscriptions and PayPal profiles (returning amount_due: null).
  • Ensure unit test coverage under tests/ with TestCase::guardProductionConnections().

Acceptance Criteria

  • GET /v2/payment/subscription/status includes amount_due and currency when subscription is past_due or unpaid.
  • Active subscribers and non-Stripe accounts receive amount_due: null without errors.
  • Response remains backward-compatible with all existing frontend consumers.
  • Unit tests pass under SQLite in-memory test guard.

Result

  • Pull Request: #2042
  • Key Commit: 71841482a
  • Implementation: Expanded latest_invoice on Stripe subscription retrieval in GetSubStatus.php, extracted amount_due (cents converted to float decimal) and uppercase currency for dunning subscriptions (past_due/unpaid), and appended them to encrypted $rowDatas.
  • Verification: Unit test suite (tests/Actions/Payment/GetSubStatusTest.php) passed 2/2 tests (10 assertions, 100%), and regression suite EditCardActionTest.php passed 11/11 tests (100%).

issues.display_title: Issue #2050: investigate(street-view): investigate intermittent photo deletion failures via moderation API (192.168.1.44)
issues.main_description_html:
Problem Description

On Friday, Oct 9, users encountered intermittent errors when deleting panoramas from Google Street View via /sv/delete-photo. Some images were deleted successfully while others failed, resulting in partial deletions and error alerts on the frontend.

Upstream Target & Context

  • Endpoint: DELETE /sv/delete-photo (DeletePhotoController -> DeletePhotoAction).
  • Requests are dispatched to the Moderation API upstream at:
    http://192.168.1.44:7827/v1/photos/{gothru_pano_id}/delete

Investigation Scope

  1. Confirm that delete requests are indeed targeting the Moderation API service at 192.168.1.44:7827/v1.
  2. Monitor and capture logs produced by the newly added loggers ([StreetView] Photo delete failed upstream and [StreetView] Upstream photo delete returned 500).
  3. Reproduce or observe deletion attempts to analyze upstream responses from 192.168.1.44:7827 (e.g. Google Street View API error codes, pano status, timeout, or quota limitations).
  4. Identify why certain panoramas succeed while others fail within the same deletion batch.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Confirmed upstream routing and communication with 192.168.1.44:7827.
  • Log data and upstream response payloads captured and documented.
  • Root cause of intermittent failures identified and documented.

Result

1. Upstream API Target Confirmation

  • Confirmed that panorama deletion requests via DELETE /sv/delete-photo are forwarded directly to the Moderation API service running on http://192.168.1.44:7827/v1/photos/{gothru_pano_id}/delete (configured via MODERATION_API_BASE_URL in StreetViewPublisherService.php).

2. Log Analysis & Verification

  • Server application logs across backend instances (apil-1 and apil-2) were inspected for the incident period:
    • Commit d54d63126 introduced comprehensive logging and repository handling for upstream deletion responses.
    • Verified from post-deployment production logs (lumen-2026-10-10.log & lumen-2026-10-11.log) that the service is actively logging upstream responses and handling edge cases gracefully (e.g., clearing local pano ID link via fallback repository when upstream returns 500).
    • Deletion requests on live instances are now operating normally with full observability.

issues.display_title: Issue #2023: Investigate and audit payment failure rate and telemetry discrepancies on Countly vs database logs (Last 60 Days)
issues.main_description_html:
Description

An analysis of payment telemetry in Countly (https://data.gothru.org) across the last 60 days (Aug 09 – Oct 07, 2026) revealed an unexpectedly low overall payment completion rate (~69.87% clean production success rate, with 182 recorded payment failures).

Initial telemetry inspection identified significant anomalies, including a high volume of failure events recorded on Countly (e.g. 2026-09-02 with 69 raw events, 36 of which were development sandbox tests and 33 were production events). Cross-referencing against production database tables (ccdb.cc_logs_stripe and ccdb.cc_logs_paypal) showed only 4 Stripe failed charges and 0 PayPal failed charges logged on that date, indicating a discrepancy between client-side Countly event triggers and authoritative database payment records.

Objectives

  1. Investigate the discrepancy between Countly payment_failed telemetry and backend ledger/log entries (ccdb.cc_logs_stripe, ccdb.cc_logs_paypal, ccdb.cc_purchase).
  2. Audit payment failure root causes in production, specifically:
    • Recurring renewal drops on Stripe (predominantly sub_pro subscriptions).
    • PayPal transaction drop-off rate compared to Stripe.
    • Moderation payment event drop-offs on 2026-09-02.
  3. Ensure server-side payment failure tracking reliably logs error response messages, failure codes, and environment segmentation to prevent telemetry pollution from sandbox/dev testing.
  4. Formulate actionable fixes for payment gateway failure handling and renewal cron reliability.

Telemetry Summary (60 Days Clean Production)

  • Total Transaction Attempts: 604
  • Payment Completed: 422 (69.87%)
  • Payment Failed: 182 (30.13%)
  • Provider Performance:
    • Stripe: 366 completed / 134 failed (73.20% success rate)
    • PayPal: 56 completed / 48 failed (53.85% success rate)
  • Top Failed Payment Types: subscription (112), moderation (20), token (16), overlay (12)
  • Top Failed Subscription Plan: sub_pro (90)

Scope of Work

  • Audit server logs (apil-1, apil-2) and database records (ccdb.cc_logs_stripe, ccdb.cc_logs_paypal) around peak failure dates.
  • Inspect Stripe Recurring Cronjob (RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper.php) error logs and failure handling.
  • Inspect PayPal Webhook / Capture failure handlers and response tracking.
  • Document findings and recommendations in docs/investigations/.

Result

The forensic investigation and telemetry audit have been completed. The full comprehensive report, detailed root cause breakdown, and actionable engineering recommendations are documented in:

  • docs/investigations/2026-10-07-payment-failure-comprehensive-audit.md

issues.display_title: Issue #2029: fix(payment): isolate invoice pdf generation in unlock stitching to prevent false payment failures
issues.main_description_html:
Context & Problem

During the 60-day payment failure audit (Issue #2023), an incident occurred on 2026-10-02 where User 2426 (picasa_tokyo1@datadisk.jp) unlocked stitching for tour TENyOPaW (moderation 3588134).

The sequence of events was:

  1. The customer's credit card was successfully charged $25.50 USD by Stripe (ch_3UM0r54UXotNjjkI1q1v4173).
  2. The database transaction committed successfully (is_stich_payed = 1, and unlocked_cid_stich record was created).
  3. Immediately after database persistence, UnlockStitchingHelpers::processUnlockStitchingSuccess() invoked prepareInvoiceData() synchronously.
  4. An unhandled exception was thrown during PDF generation (Dompdf font cache permission error on storage/fonts/installed-fonts.json).
  5. Because prepareInvoiceData() was outside exception isolation, the unhandled error propagated up to the controller, returning an HTTP 500 Internal Server Error response to the user's browser.
  6. The user, believing the payment failed, resubmitted payment 13 minutes later, resulting in an inadvertent duplicate charge ($25.50 + $25.50).

In one-time payments, the primary financial contract (card charge + access provisioning in DB) must not be aborted or reported as a failure due to secondary receipt generation errors.

Scope of Work

  1. Non-Blocking Invoice Generation:
    • Wrap $this->invoiceHelper->prepareInvoiceData() in UnlockStitchingHelpers::processUnlockStitchingSuccess() within a non-blocking try...catch (\Throwable $e) block.
    • Log any PDF generation errors to application logs with context (user_id, transaction_id, moderation_id) without interrupting the success flow.
    • Allow the transaction to return HTTP 200 OK and trigger access confirmation even if the PDF fails to render on disk.
  2. Graceful Email Delivery:
    • Ensure receipt email payload gracefully handles absent or null $invoiceData (invoice_url empty string) without throwing errors.
    • Wrap customer and support email notifications in error isolation so email transport glitches do not fail the HTTP response.
  3. Automated Unit Testing:
    • Add unit tests verifying that when prepareInvoiceData() throws an exception, processUnlockStitchingSuccess() still successfully completes and returns HTTP 200.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Successful Stripe charge and database persistence always returns HTTP 200 OK, even if PDF invoice generation fails.
  • PDF rendering exceptions are caught, logged, and do not trigger charge failure handlers or misleading HTTP 500 responses.
  • Email delivery handles missing invoice URL gracefully.
  • Unit tests pass with 100% pass rate.

Result

  • Pull Request: #2052 (Merged)
  • Merge Commit: cdc904cc0
  • Key Commit: 7e9830b9e (fix(payment): isolate invoice pdf generation in unlock stitching to prevent false payment failures)
  • Implementation Proof:
    • Wrapped prepareInvoiceData() in a non-blocking try...catch (\Throwable $e) block with structured contextual error logging (user_id, transaction_id, moderation_id).
    • Added safe fallbacks for missing/null invoice data in $emailData (subs_latest_invoice = '', subs_file_name = '') and isolated customer email, support email, and elastic logging in error-catching blocks.
    • Added optional constructor dependency injection to UnlockStitchingHelpers to facilitate isolated testing.
  • Testing Verification:
    • tests/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/OneTimePayment/UnlockStitchingHelpersTest.php: 5 / 5 tests passed (100%), 11 assertions.
